rules.title: Preliminary notice due within 20 days of first furnishing
rules.plain_english: Subcontractors and material suppliers must serve a preliminary notice no later than 20 days after they first furnish labor or materials to the job. One notice covers the whole job no matter how many deliveries are made.

parameters.trigger: claimant first furnishes labor, service, equipment, or material to the work of improvement

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors, sub-subcontractors, material suppliers and equipment lessors on private works of improvement in California (not laborers; see prelim-notice-who-is-exempt)
rules.source_location: PDF page 75 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: Within 20 days from first furnishing labor or materials, serve a "Preliminary 20-day Notice" on the owner, the original contractor, and construction lender. No matter how many deliveries you make, or the time span over which you furnish labor or materials, only one Preliminary Notice is required.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Statutory text per leginfo excerpt of Civ. Code 8204(a): 'A preliminary notice shall be given not later than 20 days after the claimant has first furnished work on the work of improvement.' The law book's '20-day' label is the pre-2012 name; the statute now calls it simply 'preliminary notice'. A claimant furnishing under contracts with more than one subcontractor may need a separate notice per contract (Civ. Code 8206) - not verified against text.

rules.title: Late preliminary notice only protects last 20 days of work
rules.plain_english: You can still serve a preliminary notice after the 20-day window, but your lien, stop payment notice and bond rights then cover only work furnished within the 20 days before you served it and anything after.

parameters.protected_work: work furnished on or after (service_date - 20 days)

rules.applies_to: Claimants required to give preliminary notice on private works
rules.verbatim_quote: The Preliminary Notice may be delivered in person or by certified, registered, or first class mail before work begins or supplies are delivered and up to 20 days thereafter. Notice may be given after those 20 days, but payment only is required for work done 20 days before the notice is delivered and anytime thereafter.
rules.notes: CSLB consumer page summary. Leginfo excerpt of 8204: 'The claimant shall, however, be entitled to record a lien, give a stop payment notice, and assert a claim against a payment bond only for work performed within 20 days prior to the service of the preliminary notice, and at any time thereafter.' CSLB's mention of 'first class mail' conflicts with the current Civ. Code 8110 mail methods (registered, certified, express or overnight); see notice-service-methods.

rules.title: Who does not need to give preliminary notice
rules.plain_english: Laborers do not need to give preliminary notice. A direct (prime) contractor that contracts with the owner does not send one to the owner, but must send one to the construction lender if the job has a construction loan.
rules.applies_to: Private works of improvement
rules.verbatim_quote: NOTE: This notice is not required from laborers or the direct contractor.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8200: '(1) A laborer is not required to give preliminary notice. (2) A claimant with a direct contractual relationship with an owner or reputed owner is required to give preliminary notice only to the construction lender or reputed construction lender, if any.' CSLB homeowner guide (https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/HomeownersGuideToPreventingMechanicsLiens.pdf): 'The prime contractor must provide a Preliminary Notice to the construction lender if the contracted project is being financed by a loan.'

rules.title: No preliminary notice = no lien / stop notice rights
rules.plain_english: If a subcontractor or supplier who is required to serve a preliminary notice does not do so, it loses the right to record a mechanics lien, serve a stop payment notice, or claim on a payment bond (except as allowed by the bond-notice rules).

parameters.consequence_of_no_notice: lien, stop payment notice and (generally) bond rights unenforceable

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and suppliers on private works
rules.verbatim_quote: If subcontractors and suppliers don't provide you with the notice, they lose the right to file a lien.
rules.notes: Leginfo excerpt of 8200 (search snippet): compliance 'is a necessary prerequisite to the validity of a lien claim or stop payment notice'. For payment bonds, a claimant without preliminary notice can still give the 15/75-day bond notice under Civ. Code 8612 (see private-bond-claim-notice).

rules.title: Preliminary notice required contents
rules.plain_english: The preliminary notice must contain the general notice information (owner, direct contractor, lender, site description, who is giving the notice), a general description of the work, an estimate of the total price, and the statutory 'Notice to Property Owner' warning, including wording telling the owner it must notify preliminary-notice givers if it records a notice of completion or cessation.

fields: construction lender name and address (if any)
site description sufficient for identification (street address if any)
name, address and relationship of person giving notice
general description of work to be provided
name of person to or for whom the work is provided
estimate of total price of the work
parameters.owner_warning_type: boldface (point size per statute; not verified)

rules.applies_to: Claimants preparing preliminary notices on private works
rules.source_location: PDF page 75 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: The notice must include specific wording to inform a property owner of a new responsibility to notify anyone else who served a Preliminary Notice.

rules.title: Optional: file preliminary notice with county recorder
rules.plain_english: A claimant may also file its preliminary notice with the county recorder where the property is located; the recorder will then notify the claimant when a notice of completion or cessation is recorded on that property.

parameters.where: county recorder of county where site is located
parameters.benefit: recorder mails notification of recorded notice of completion/cessation

rules.citation: Civil Code 8200-8216 (filing with county recorder; exact section not verified)

rules.verbatim_quote: NOTE: You may also file the Preliminary 20-day Notice with the county recorder in the county in which the property is located. The county recorder will then notify you when a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded on the property.
rules.notes: CSLB Law Book narrative; statutory section number for recorder filing not confirmed (believed to be in Civ. Code 8200-8216).

rules.title: Subcontractor discipline for skipping preliminary notice
rules.plain_english: A licensed subcontractor who is required to give preliminary notice and fails to do so on a subcontract over $400 can be disciplined by the CSLB.
rules.applies_to: Licensed subcontractors on private works

rules.title: Allowed methods to serve lien-law notices
rules.plain_english: Lien-law notices (preliminary notice, stop payment notice, bond notice, etc.) must be given by personal delivery, by registered or certified mail, express mail, or overnight express carrier, or by leaving the notice and mailing a copy as in CCP 415.20. Plain first-class mail alone is not a listed method.

methods: overnight delivery by express service carrier
leave notice and mail copy per CCP 415.20 (not verified)
parameters.mail_service_complete: when deposited in the mail or with express carrier per CCP 1013

rules.applies_to: All notices under Civil Code Part 6 (private and public works)
rules.verbatim_quote: notice by mail under this part shall be given by registered or certified mail, express mail, or overnight delivery by an express service carrier
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. rules.title: Proof of notice declaration and mailing receipts
rules.plain_english: Keep a signed declaration of service for every notice, stating what was served, when, where and how; for mailed notices attach the USPS registered/certified/express receipt or the express carrier's tracking record.

declaration_contents: date, place and manner of notice
facts showing notice was given as required
name and address of person notified
title or capacity of person notified (if any)
parameters.mail_attachment: USPS documentation showing payment for registered/certified/express mail, or express carrier tracking record

rules.applies_to: Anyone giving lien-law notices
rules.verbatim_quote: documentation provided by the United States Postal Service showing that payment was made to mail the notice using registered or certified mail, or express mail

rules.title: When a private work of improvement is 'complete'
rules.plain_english: For lien deadlines, completion happens on the earliest of: actual completion; owner occupation or use plus cessation of labor; cessation of labor for 60 continuous days; or recording a notice of cessation after 30 continuous days of no labor. Public-entity jobs are complete on acceptance.

triggers: owner occupation or use accompanied by cessation of labor
cessation of labor for continuous 60 days
recordation of notice of cessation after cessation of labor for continuous 30 days

rules.applies_to: Private works (Civil Code Title 2)
rules.verbatim_quote: If a work of improvement is subject to acceptance by a public entity, completion occurs on acceptance.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. The 30-day notice-of-cessation trigger was seen in SB 189 bill text and is consistent with the Law Book ('Labor must have ceased for at least 30 days before the owner is entitled to record a Notice of Cessation', PDF page 75) but was not confirmed in the codified excerpt.

rules.title: Notice of completion must be recorded within 15 days of completion
rules.plain_english: An owner who wants the shorter lien deadlines must record a notice of completion with the county recorder within 15 days after the date of completion; a late notice is ineffective.

parameters.who: owner (signed and verified by owner or owner's agent)
parameters.where: county recorder of county where site is located

rules.applies_to: Owners of private works; direct contractors assisting owners
rules.verbatim_quote: Filing a Notice of Completion with the county recorder's office after work is completed reduces the amount of time a contractor, subcontractor, laborer, or materials supplier has to record a claim. Homeowners have 15 days from the date of completion to do so.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. CONFLICT: the 2026 CSLB Law Book glossary (PDF page 80) still says 'within 10 days after completion' - that is the pre-2012 rule; use 15 days.

rules.title: Notice of completion contents
rules.plain_english: A notice of completion is signed and verified by the owner or its agent and states the completion date, owner name and address, the owner's interest, the site address or description, and the name of the original (direct) contractor.

fields: nature of owner's interest or estate
site street address or description sufficient for identification
name of original/direct contractor for the work completed

rules.applies_to: Owners recording notices of completion on private works
rules.source_location: PDF page 79 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: Notice of Completion is a written notice, signed and verified by the owner or their agent, stating: 1. Date that the job was finished. 2. Name and address of the owner. 3. Nature of the interest or estate of the owner.
rules.notes: Law Book glossary list continues: '4. Street address of the site, if any, or a description of the site sufficient for identification. 5. Name of the original contractor, if any, for the contract covering the portion of the work of improvement completed.' The same glossary's '10 days' recording period is outdated (see noc-recording-15-days).

rules.title: Notice of cessation: 30 days of no labor first
rules.plain_english: An owner may record a notice of cessation only after labor has stopped for at least 30 continuous days; the notice states when labor stopped and that none has been performed since, plus owner, site and contractor details.
rules.applies_to: Owners of private works
rules.citation: Civil Code 8180, 8188 (section number for notice of cessation not verified)
rules.source_location: PDF page 75 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: Labor must have ceased for at least 30 days before the owner is entitled to record a Notice of Cessation.
rules.notes: Contents per Law Book glossary (PDF page 79): 'Notice of Cessation is a written notice, signed and verified by the owner or their agent, stating: 1. Approximate date when labor on the job stopped. 2. Confirmation that no further labor has been performed since the recording of the notice...'.

rules.title: Owner must send copy of recorded NOC/cessation within 10 days
rules.plain_english: An owner who records a notice of completion or cessation must, within 10 days of recording, send a copy to the direct contractor and to every claimant who served it a preliminary notice. If it doesn't, the notice does not shorten that person's lien deadline. Owner-occupants of 1-4 unit residences are excluded.

parameters.trigger: date notice of completion or cessation is recorded
recipients: each claimant that gave the owner preliminary notice
parameters.consequence_of_failure: notice ineffective to shorten that person's time to record under 8412/8414 (stays 90 days)
parameters.exempt: owner occupying the property as a personal residence with four or fewer units

rules.applies_to: Owners of private works recording notices of completion or cessation
rules.source_location: PDF page 76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: NOTE: An owner who files a Notice of Cessation or a Notice of Completion must notify any potential lien claimants within 10 days of recording the notices. This notification is designed to let you, the potential lien claimant, know that the time for filing a Claim of Lien has been reduced.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. rules.title: Direct contractor lien recording deadline (60/90 days)
rules.plain_english: A direct (prime) contractor records its lien after it completes its contract and no later than 60 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation, or 90 days after completion of the whole job if no valid notice is recorded - whichever is earlier.

parameters.earliest: after completion of the direct contract

rules.applies_to: Direct (prime/original) contractors on private works
rules.source_location: PDF page 77 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: 1. Within 60 days of recording a Notice of Cessation or a Notice of Completion, the contractor must record a Claim of Lien.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. rules.title: Subcontractor/supplier lien recording deadline (30/90 days)
rules.plain_english: Subcontractors, suppliers and other non-direct claimants must record their lien no later than 30 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation, or 90 days after completion if no valid notice is recorded - whichever is earlier.
rules.applies_to: Subcontractors, material suppliers, equipment lessors, laborers on private works
rules.source_location: PDF page 75-76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Within 30 days of the owner recording either a Notice of Cessation or Completion, the subcontractor must record a Claim of Lien with the county recorder.

rules.title: No NOC recorded: 90 days after completion/use/acceptance
rules.plain_english: If no notice of completion or cessation is recorded, any claimant has 90 days after completion - including when labor ceases and the owner uses the improvement, or the owner accepts it - to record its lien.

triggers: labor ceases and owner/agent uses improvement

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.verbatim_quote: The potential lien claimant must record the mechanics lien within 90 days of: Completion of work; When the property owner began using the improvement;* or When the property owner accepted the improvement.
rules.notes: CSLB consumer page. Same rule appears in Law Book checklist (PDF page 76-77). Note completion also occurs automatically after 60 continuous days of no labor (Civ. Code 8180).

rules.title: Lien foreclosure suit within 90 days of recording
rules.plain_english: After recording a mechanics lien, the claimant must file a lawsuit to foreclose it within 90 days (and record a lis pendens); otherwise the lien expires and is unenforceable.

parameters.also_record: lis pendens (notice of pendency of action)

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.source_location: PDF page 76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) File Lien Foreclosure Action within 90 days of recording a Claim of Lien and record a lis pendens at the same time. You must also file an action on the stop notice at this time, if applicable.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. rules.title: Credit extension can extend foreclosure deadline (max 1 year after completion)
rules.plain_english: If the owner and claimant agree to extend credit and record notice of the extension, the foreclosure suit is due within 90 days after the credit expires, but never later than one year after completion of the work.

parameters.absolute_limit: 1 year after completion of work of improvement

rules.applies_to: Private-works lien claimants granting credit to owner
rules.verbatim_quote: the claimant shall commence an action to enforce the lien within 90 days after the expiration of the credit, but in no case later than one year after completion of the work of improvement

rules.title: Claim of mechanics lien required contents
rules.plain_english: The claim of lien must be signed and verified and state: the amount owed after credits and offsets, the owner's name, the kind of work or materials furnished, who hired you, a site description, and your address, plus the Notice of Mechanics Lien and a proof of service affidavit.

fields: amount of demand after deducting credits and offsets
name of owner or reputed owner, if known
kind of labor, service, equipment or materials furnished
name of person who employed claimant or to whom work was furnished
description of site sufficient for identification
Notice of Mechanics Lien (statutory text, at least 10-point boldface)

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.source_location: PDF page 78 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: Claim of Lien (mechanics lien) is a written statement signed and verified by the claimant or by the claimant's agent that must state the following: 1. The amount of claimant's demand (after deducting credits and offsets). 2. The name of the owner or reputed owner, if known.
rules.notes: Law Book glossary (PDF page 78) also lists items 3-5 (kind of labor, person who employed claimant, site description). rules.title: Serve lien + Notice of Mechanics Lien with proof of service affidavit
rules.plain_english: A copy of the recorded lien with the Notice of Mechanics Lien must be served on the owner (or, if the owner can't be served, on the construction lender or direct contractor), and the server must sign a proof of service affidavit. Failure makes the lien unenforceable.

affidavit_contents: date, place and manner of service
name and address of person served and capacity

rules.source_location: PDF page 78 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: Failure to serve the mechanics lien and confirm a proof of service affidavit will cause the mechanics lien to be unenforceable.

rules.title: Lien only for work incorporated; supplier's supplier has no lien
rules.plain_english: To have a lien, your labor or materials must be incorporated (installed) in the improvement, and you must have been hired by the owner or someone in charge of the work; a supplier to a material supplier has no statutory lien.
rules.applies_to: Potential lien claimants on private works
rules.citation: Cal. Const. art. XIV, sec. 3; Civil Code 8400, 8404
rules.source_location: PDF page 73 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: A material supplier is not the agent of the owner and, therefore, a material supplier's supplier is not entitled to a statutory lien. Further, to perfect your lien, the work and/or materials, etc. must be incorporated into the structure. That is to say, it has to be installed.
rules.notes: CSLB Law Book narrative. The statute (8400, 8404) not fetched; incorporation requirement is the Law Book's characterization.

rules.title: Unlicensed contractor cannot enforce lien over $500
rules.plain_english: Anyone can record a lien, but an unlicensed contractor cannot foreclose a mechanics lien for work valued over $500 (B&P 7031 bars suits for compensation).

parameters.condition: work requiring a license performed while unlicensed

rules.applies_to: Contractors performing work requiring a CSLB license
rules.verbatim_quote: Although anyone can record a mechanics lien, unlicensed contractors cannot foreclose on a mechanics lien if the work is valued at more than $500.
rules.notes: CSLB consumer page. The $500 figure corresponds to the minor-work exemption (B&P 7048); see license-domain research for 7031/7048 details.

rules.title: Lien release bond = 125% of claim
rules.plain_english: An owner, direct contractor or affected subcontractor can free the property from a recorded lien by recording a release bond from an admitted surety equal to 125% of the lien amount (or of the amount allocated to the property released).
rules.applies_to: Private works with recorded mechanics liens
rules.verbatim_quote: 125 percent of the amount of the claim of lien or 125 percent of the amount allocated in the claim of lien to the real property to be released

rules.title: Release-order petition: 10-day demand first
rules.plain_english: If the claimant has not filed a foreclosure suit within the 90-day period, the owner can petition the court to release the lien, but must first send the claimant a demand to release the lien at least 10 days before filing.

parameters.precondition: no enforcement action within Civ. Code 8460 period
parameters.demand_content: demand that claimant execute and record a release of the claim of lien

rules.applies_to: Owners of private property with expired/unenforced liens
rules.verbatim_quote: unless at least 10 days before filing the petition the owner gives the claimant notice demanding that the claimant execute and record a release of the claim of lien
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. rules.title: Prevailing party attorney fees on lien release petition (no cap)
rules.plain_english: In a court petition to release a lien, the prevailing party gets reasonable attorney's fees; the old $2,000 cap was removed effective July 1, 2012.
rules.applies_to: Owners and lien claimants in release-order proceedings
rules.verbatim_quote: Civil Code section 8488 provides that if you use an attorney and you prevail, you are entitled to reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.notes: CSLB homeowner guide (PDF columns extracted with pdftotext; quote text read from guide). Leginfo excerpt of 8488: 'The prevailing party is entitled to reasonable attorney's fees.' 8488 also puts the burden of proof as to lien validity on the claimant.

rules.title: Notice of nonresponsibility: post and record within 10 days
rules.plain_english: An owner who did not order the work (e.g., a landlord whose tenant is remodeling) can avoid lien liability only by posting a signed, verified notice of nonresponsibility on the site and recording it within 10 days after learning of the work.

rules.title: Home improvement downpayment: lesser of $1,000 or 10%
rules.plain_english: On a home improvement contract, any downpayment may not exceed $1,000 or 10% of the contract amount, whichever is less.

rules.plain_english: Except for the downpayment, a home improvement contractor may not request or accept payment that exceeds the value of the work performed or materials delivered, including advance payments from a lender.

rules.title: Schedule of progress payments in dollars and cents
rules.plain_english: If any payments besides the downpayment are due before completion, the home improvement contract must include a 'Schedule of Progress Payments' stating each payment in dollars and cents tied to specific work, materials and equipment, with the statutory 12-point boldface warning.

rules.title: HIC must include the 'Mechanics Lien Warning' notice
rules.plain_english: Home improvement contracts must include the statutory 'Mechanics Lien Warning' explaining liens, preliminary notices, the 20-day timing, and joint checks (unless the contractor furnishes qualifying bonds or joint control).
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source_location: PDF page 402 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: Anyone who helps improve your property, but who is not paid, may record what is called a mechanics lien on your property. A mechanics lien is a claim, like a mortgage or home equity loan, made against your property and recorded with the county recorder.
rules.notes: Full text runs on Law Book PDF pages 402-403 (7159(e)(4)); generator should copy the entire warning verbatim from the Law Book including 'BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work...' and the CSLB contact line. 7159(e) allows attachment only where a paragraph expressly authorizes it; paragraph (4) does not, so treat the warning as part of the contract form.

rules.title: Bond/joint-control exemption from HIC payment limits
rules.plain_english: A contractor that furnishes a performance and payment bond, lien and completion bond, CSLB-approved bond equivalent, or joint control covering full performance and payment is exempt from the downpayment, payment-schedule and no-advance-payment rules and the Mechanics Lien Warning, and may accept payment before completion. A blanket bond application requires 2 years of active licensure.

rules.source_location: PDF page 411 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: A contractor furnishing these bonds, bond equivalents, or a joint control approved by the registrar may accept payment prior to completion.
rules.notes: Contractor furnishing joint control may not have a financial or other interest in the joint control.

rules.title: HIC payment violations are misdemeanors ($100-$5,000)
rules.plain_english: Violating the written-contract-amount, downpayment cap, or no-payment-ahead-of-work rules is a misdemeanor: fine of $100 to $5,000, up to 1 year in county jail, or both; the maximum fine is mandatory in declared disaster areas.
